title: Audit logs: include authz decision context + policy version identifiers
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes:
- Audit log events now optionally include `authz_*` fields describing the authorization decision for the triggering request.
- Adds `authz_policy_bundle_version` and `authz_policy_revision` identifiers to support evidence and incident forensics.
- No schema hard-break: fields are additive and omitted when authz context is unavailable (e.g., legacy emitters / background jobs).
body:
## Summary
This PR extends audit log events emitted by Redwood services (API Gateway + Control Plane) to include authorization decision context when available. The goal is to make authorization enforcement auditable (SOC2 evidence, enterprise questionnaires) and to support debugging/forensics ("who attempted what", "why denied", "which policy version was evaluated").

This is intentionally additive: existing event consumers continue to work without changes. Fields are only populated when we have a request-scoped authz evaluation result.

## Motivation / context
RBAC v2 rollout requires: (1) deny-by-default enforcement, and (2) evidence-friendly audit artifacts that tie an audited action to an explicit authz decision and policy version. Several enterprise prospects asked for examples of audit entries containing allow/deny, subject identity, scoped resource, and policy version identifiers.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-18339
- RBAC v2 audit logging requirements (Security/Compliance)

## What changed
### 1) Audit event schema (additive)
Adds the following optional fields to the audit event envelope:
- `authz_decision`: `ALLOW` | `DENY`
- `authz_subject_type`: `USER` | `API_KEY` | `SERVICE`
- `authz_subject_id`: stable identifier (no emails/usernames)
- `authz_action`: canonical permission string (e.g., `org.api_keys.rotate`)
- `authz_resource_type`: canonical resource type (e.g., `org`, `project`, `deployment`, `audit_log`)
- `authz_resource_id`: resource identifier when available
- `authz_scope`: normalized scope string (e.g., `org:o_123`, `project:p_456`, `env:e_prod`, `cluster:c_01`)
- `authz_policy_bundle_version`: policy bundle version (e.g., `rbac-bundle@2025.02.24`)
- `authz_policy_revision`: internal monotonically increasing revision/etag for the evaluated policy snapshot
- `authz_denial_reason_codes`: comma-separated list of standardized reason codes (e.g., `MISSING_PERMISSION,SCOPE_MISMATCH`)
- `authz_eval_source`: `gateway` | `service`
- `authz_cache_hit`: `true` | `false` (stringified in the logger layer)
- `authz_eval_latency_ms`: integer ms serialized as string

### 2) Request context propagation
- Plumbs `AuthzDecisionContext` through the request context used by the audit logger.
- Gateway emitters attach authz context for request-driven audit events.
- Control Plane emitters attach authz context for request-driven events and leave it empty for job-driven events.

### 3) Redaction / privacy
- No raw tokens, no group membership lists, no evaluated policy content.
- `authz_subject_id` is the internal principal id; we do not log email.
- `authz_scope` is normalized and does not include customer-provided freeform names.

## Example event (illustrative)
Before:
- `action=api_key.rotate`, `actor_id=u_1a2b`, `org_id=o_123`

After (new fields added, not replacing existing ones):
- `action=api_key.rotate`
- `authz_decision=ALLOW`
- `authz_subject_type=USER`
- `authz_subject_id=u_1a2b`
- `authz_action=org.api_keys.rotate`
- `authz_resource_type=org`
- `authz_resource_id=o_123`
- `authz_scope=org:o_123`
- `authz_policy_bundle_version=rbac-bundle@2025.02.24`
- `authz_policy_revision=rev_9c4f3d`
- `authz_eval_source=gateway`
- `authz_cache_hit=true`
- `authz_eval_latency_ms=1`

Denied example:
- `authz_decision=DENY`
- `authz_denial_reason_codes=MISSING_PERMISSION`

## Testing
- Unit tests: schema serialization, optional field behavior, and redaction rules
- Integration tests: gateway request -> audit event includes authz fields for allow + deny paths
- Verified: audit-log exporter continues to ingest events with extra fields (no consumer-side break)

## Rollout / compatibility notes
- Additive fields only; downstream systems should treat unknown fields as ignorable.
- Events emitted outside request context (periodic jobs, async processors) will not contain `authz_*` fields until those emitters are updated to explicitly attach authz context.

## Follow-ups
- Update audit-log exporter mapping to SIEM schemas to include these fields (separate PR)
- Align denial reason code taxonomy with Console "why denied" UX (in-flight)

## Checklist
- [x] Add schema fields in shared audit event envelope
- [x] Ensure fields are optional and omitted by default
- [x] Add request-context plumbing for gateway + control plane
- [x] Add tests + example fixtures
- [x] Security review for redaction and PII
commits: auditlog: extend event envelope with authz decision fields
gateway: attach AuthzDecisionContext to request-scoped audit logger
control-plane: propagate authz context into audit events where available
auditlog: add serialization tests + golden fixtures
docs: internal notes on new authz audit fields
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we confirm no user emails leak into `authz_subject_id`? Also please document which emitters will not have authz context (jobs).

Kevin Osei (author): Confirmed. `authz_subject_id` comes from principal id (u_*/k_*/svc_*). Added a note in the PR body and a unit test ensuring email is never serialized. Jobs will omit `authz_*` until follow-up updates.
Allison Grant (review): `authz_eval_latency_ms` and `authz_cache_hit` as strings feels odd. Can we keep them typed?

Kevin Osei (author): Our JSON audit envelope is stringly-typed for historical reasons (proto->json bridge + ingestion pipeline). Kept consistent with existing fields to avoid consumer parsing surprises. Added comments + tests.
Jordan Lee (review): Please ensure `authz_policy_bundle_version` is stable and matches the policy bundle artifact version, not git SHA from runtime.
Kevin Osei (author): Updated to use bundle release version from the evaluator client (`rbac-bundle@YYYY.MM.DD`) plus a separate internal `authz_policy_revision` (etag) for the snapshot.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Do we log denial reason codes for all denies? Some denies happen before evaluation (missing authn).

Kevin Osei (author): Only for completed authz evaluations. Authn failures continue to be logged via existing error fields. Added `authz_denial_reason_codes` as optional and clarified in code comments.
Marcus Lin (approve): Approved after PII test + policy version stabilization.
notes: Coordinated with Security & Compliance on field names; follow-up work will update SIEM exporter mappings and customer-facing documentation examples.
